executiveSummary: Surveillance data from ECDC and PAHO spanning October 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent biological threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) continues to pose an elevated zoonotic threat in the Americas with ongoing animal-to-human spillover risk, representing a BSL-3 select agent of significant concern. Dengue, mpox, yellow fever, and chikungunya are circulating simultaneously in the Americas, straining regional health systems. Respiratory threats including seasonal influenza, RSV, and pertussis show resurgence patterns in both hemispheres, while measles importation risk persists due to vaccination gaps.
bottomLine: The Americas face a complex multi-pathogen emergency led by H5N1 zoonotic spillover risk and simultaneous arboviral surges, requiring coordinated One Health surveillance and emergency response capacity.

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents are under active surveillance in this reporting period. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) — a Tier 1 select agent with pandemic potential — prompted PAHO epidemiological updates in November 2025 and March 2026, indicating sustained zoonotic circulation in the Americas with human spillover risk. Monkeypox virus (MPXV) — a BSL-3 select agent — prompted a PAHO update in April 2026 confirming ongoing transmission in the Americas. Both pathogens require BSL-3 containment for diagnostic and research activities and demand heightened biosurveillance and international coordination.
amrSignals: No explicit AMR reports identified in current surveillance set; however, Bordetella pertussis macrolide resistance should be monitored given multi-wave resurgence patterns
Ongoing pertussis resurgence despite vaccination coverage warrants investigation into potential pathogen adaptation rather than solely vaccine-driven immunity gaps
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen burden in the Americas spanning arboviruses, zoonoses, and vaccine-preventable diseases suggests systemic surveillance and immunization system stress
Southern Hemisphere influenza season 2026 onset coinciding with residual RSV circulation creates compounding respiratory emergency risk
Repeated PAHO pertussis alerts across consecutive months indicate failure of current control measures and possible waning vaccine immunity at population level
H5N1 sustained circulation in the Americas across two separate reporting periods (Nov 2025 and Mar 2026) suggests endemic establishment in wild bird and mammal reservoirs
Mpox persistence in the Americas despite prior vaccination campaigns raises concern for ongoing transmission networks in specific risk populations
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert from PAHO (Feb 2026) signals emerging non-communicable public health risk intersecting with communicable disease response capacity
Methanol poisoning alert (Oct 2025) indicates parallel chemical safety threats requiring health system attention alongside biological threats
